title: Protein Conformation Generation via Force-Guided SE(3) Diffusion Models

nodes.text: CONFDIFF is a force-guided SE(3) diffusion model for protein conformation generation that combines a force-guidance network with a mixture of data-based score models to produce diverse yet high-fidelity conformations.
nodes.evidence: we propose a force-guided SE(3) diffusion model, CONFDIFF, for protein conformation generation

nodes.text: Existing score-based diffusion methods cannot properly incorporate physical prior knowledge (such as the MD force field) to guide generation, causing sampled conformations to deviate substantially from the equilibrium (Boltzmann) distribution.
nodes.evidence: existing score-based diffusion methods cannot properly incorporate important physical prior knowledge to guide the generation process, causing large deviations in the sampled protein conformations from the equilibrium distribution

nodes.text: CONFDIFF uses classifier-free guidance on SE(3), combining a sequence-conditional score model and an unconditional score model with a guidance-strength coefficient gamma to trade off conformation quality against diversity.
nodes.evidence: we use classifier-free guidance on SE(3) to find a better trade-off between conformation quality and diversity

nodes.text: An intermediate force guidance strategy is introduced that uses an equivariant network to directly approximate the intermediate force vector during reverse-time diffusion sampling, steering generation toward lower-energy conformations.
nodes.evidence: we propose a force guidance strategy which employs an equivariant network to directly approximate the intermediate force vector

nodes.text: The MD energy function (computed via OpenMM) is used as a physics-based reward, defining a target equilibrium distribution p0(x0) proportional to q0(x0) exp(-k E0(x0)), drawing inspiration from contrastive energy prediction (CEP).
nodes.evidence: Drawing inspiration from the contrastive energy prediction (CEP) technique (Lu et al., 2023), we employ the MD energy prior as a physics-based preference function

nodes.text: Unlike DiG (Zheng et al., 2023), CONFDIFF does not rely on MD simulation data during training, instead training on PDB structures plus self-generated conformation samples.
nodes.evidence: Compared with DiG (Zheng et al., 2023), our method does not rely on MD data during training

nodes.text: Unlike Str2Str (Lu et al., 2024), CONFDIFF's guidance intensity coefficient gives a higher degree of freedom for balancing sample diversity and quality.
nodes.evidence: compared with Str2Str (Lu et al., 2024), the guidance intensity coefficient provides a higher degree of freedom for balancing sample diversity and quality

nodes.text: The force-guided network is described as the first force-guided network suitable for protein conformation generation, aligning diverse conformation predictions with the equilibrium distribution.
nodes.evidence: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first force-guided network suitable for protein conformation generation

nodes.text: DiG differs from CONFDIFF by adding a loss regularization that aligns the learned score with the MD force field at small diffusion time, extended over the pathway via the Fokker-Planck equation.
nodes.evidence: DiG incorporates an additional regularization into its loss function to align the learned score with MD force field at small diffusion time, which then extends over the entire pathway by the Fokker-Planck equation

nodes.text: MD simulations converge to the Boltzmann equilibrium distribution given enough time but suffer from femtosecond time steps, rare-event sampling, and long equilibration, making them impractical for high-throughput conformation studies.
nodes.evidence: MD simulations converge towards the equilibrium distribution (i.e., the Boltzmann distribution) given sufficient time ... the time step of MD simulations is typically only a few femtoseconds

nodes.text: The advantage of EigenFold's harmonic prior over a conventional isotropic Gaussian prior is not evidently clear, and Str2Str's lack of sequence or energy information raises doubt over whether its diverse outputs adhere to the Boltzmann distribution.
nodes.evidence: the advantage of using a harmonic prior over the conventional isotropic Gaussian prior is not evidently clear ... the absence of sequence or energy information evokes a question of whether the diverse generated outcomes adhere to the Boltzmann distribution

nodes.text: Diffusion on SE(3)^N is modeled following Yim et al. (FrameDiff) with two independent processes for the translation subspace (Gaussian) and rotation subspace (isotropic Gaussian IGSO3 on SO(3)), trained with a denoising score matching loss.
nodes.evidence: Following Yim et al. (2023b), diffusion modeling on manifold SE(3)N is employed ... Two independent diffusion processes are defined for the translation and rotation subspaces

nodes.text: On 12 fast-folding proteins and the Bovine Pancreatic Trypsin Inhibitor (BPTI), CONFDIFF surpasses the state-of-the-art, with energy and force guidance sampling lower-energy conformations that are more truthful to the Boltzmann distribution.
nodes.evidence: Experiments on a variety of protein conformation prediction tasks, including 12 fast-folding proteins and the Bovine Pancreatic Trypsin Inhibitor (BPTI), demonstrate that our method surpasses the state-of-the-art method
